precepts.text: Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently. Unfeigned: don't be fake, don't be phony.
precepts.point: So this is where you self-examine: am I being a phony, a hypocrite amongst the brethren? Am I walking feignedly? Only you can answer that. You and God know the answer; we don't. If a sister ask us, what about this brother, we can only tell her what you show us. Is he really like that? You got to talk to this guy more in depth, more personally, to find out how they truly are. And some brothers can fake it real good.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently.” Unfeigned: don't be fake, don't be phony.

Some brothers can fake it real good. If a sister asks us, what about this brother, we can only tell her what you show us. Is he really like that? She's got to talk to him more in depth, more personally, to find out how he truly is.

That is why the love of the brethren has to be unfeigned, out of a pure heart. Only you and God know whether you are walking feignedly; we only see what you show us.

precepts.text: Peter writes to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia. On the map of Asia Minor you see Ephesus, and right next to it Colosse. That is what we are dealing with today.
precepts.point: But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ. Who was afar off? Israel. These Ephesians in Ephesus are Israelites scattered in Ephesus. He is our peace: not everybody's peace. Christ is the peace that brings both nations, the southern and northern kingdom, back together.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
“Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia.” Peter writes to the strangers, and the strangers are Israel, scattered abroad.

Put the map up and focus on Asia, which is Asia Minor. There you see Ephesus, and right next to it Colosse. That is what we are dealing with: the letter to the Colossians, and since Pastor Mitchell brought up Ephesus, which is right there in Asia next to Colosse, the letter to the Ephesians too.

So the saints at Ephesus and the strangers Peter wrote to are the same people: Israelites scattered through Asia. When Paul says they were “strangers from the covenants of promise”, he is writing to scattered Israel, not to the nations.

precepts.text: Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently. Peter came back and taught it after he learned: we cannot have fake love for the brethren, because God already showed me; and when I was put to the test, I was influenced not to accept them. So now the message is: do not have feigned love for the brethren.
precepts.point: If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews? Peter knew better. He was corrected in front of them all, and he would have been embarrassed and ashamed. But he repented; and as a teacher, what do you teach after that? What you repented from: do not be fake.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
James, Cephas and John gave Paul and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship, “that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.” The heathen are the northern kingdom. Peter already knew this. God had shown him that he could not call any man common or unclean. He sat with them, and he convinced many of the Jews that these men were all right, that God had granted them repentance unto life too.

“But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed.” When certain came from James, Peter “withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision. And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation.” Dissimulation means deception, hypocrisy, pretence, deceit, fakery: in other words, being fake. Paul said to him before them all, you are being fake like they were fake. Peter knew better, and he was corrected in front of everybody. He would have been embarrassed and ashamed.

But he repented. And as a teacher, what do you teach after that? What you repented from: do not be fake. So Peter wrote “Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently”.

Peter came back and taught it after he learned it: I was wrong. We cannot have fake love for the brethren, because God already showed me, and when I was put to the test I was influenced not to accept them. So the message now is, do not have feigned love for the brethren.

precepts.text: Ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold, but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot. Christ was that lamb.
precepts.point: First the weekly Sabbath, whose true meaning we just read: rest going into the kingdom. Then the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord's passover, which we just finished celebrating, and the fifteenth day begins the feast of unleavened bread: seven days ye must eat unleavened bread. The unleavened bread is Christ's sinless life, and the haste out of Egypt besides.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Peter shows who that lamb without blemish was: “ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold, from your vain conversation received by tradition from your fathers; But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot”.

So Christ was that lamb without blemish, the same thing Exodus 12:5 required. Without blemish and without spot. He is the one “foreordained before the foundation of the world, but was manifest in these last times for you”.

That is what John the Baptist said of Christ when he saw him coming: Behold the Lamb of God that takes away the sins of the world. The passover of Leviticus 23:5 is fulfilled in him.

precepts.text: For Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel mine elect.
precepts.point: Peter writes to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia, elect according to the foreknowledge of God. Isaiah 45:4 says 'Israel mine elect.' The strangers are Israelites.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Peter writes “to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia”, and calls them “Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father”. Who are the elect? Isaiah answers it: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name”. Israel mine elect, or my chosen, same thing. So the strangers Peter is writing to are Israelites. They are the grafted in strangers, the ones called not a people, not my people, the northern kingdom.

The thought does not change in chapter 2; he is not writing to somebody else. “But ye are a chosen generation”: the “ye” is the strangers of chapter 1 verse 1, the elect of verse 2. Chosen goes back to elect. They are “a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people”, and all Israel is a peculiar people. Context matters. Against them stand “them which be disobedient”, the builders, the southern kingdom's Pharisees, Sadducees, scribes, elders and rulers, who stumbled at the stone and were appointed to it, so Christ could be killed and die for both kingdoms, to reunite all twelve tribes. That could not be done unless Christ died.

Peter is quoting Hosea. Jezreel is the seed of Israel, and God says “I will sow her unto me in the earth; and I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy; and I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people”. So Peter writes “Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God”. That promise was made to the northern kingdom in Isaiah 7 and 8 and Hosea 1. When Christ dies he redeems them back into being his people and gathers them together in one. How could you find that out if you don't know your history?

precepts.text: To the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia, elect according to the foreknowledge of God.
precepts.point: Ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
Peter writes “to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia”, and verse 2 calls them “Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through sanctification of the Spirit, unto obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ”. These strangers are the same strangers that came to keep the Passover in Chronicles, and the elect is the same name given to those called according to Hosea and Isaiah in Romans 9. Who's that? Israel.

So when verse 9 says “But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people”, the “ye” is these same strangers scattered abroad. They are set against “them which be disobedient”: the builders that disallowed the stone, the southern kingdom, the Pharisees that rejected Christ and stumbled at that stone of stumbling and rock of offence of Isaiah 8:14. They were “appointed” to it. They had to put Christ to death, and his death gave the other kingdom the chance to repent and come back into the fold. By rejecting Christ they brought back in the same brothers they rejected.

The scattered elect were called “out of darkness into his marvellous light”, which is Isaiah 9:1. And they are the ones “Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.” That goes back to Deuteronomy 32 and Isaiah 7, not a people. The northern tribes, cast off and scattered, are now the people of God.

precepts.text: The precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot, foreordained before the foundation of the world.
precepts.point: The lamb without blemish and without spot points to Christ, who was sinless, verily foreordained before the foundation of the world but manifest in these last times for the nation of Israel.

note.label: Exodus 12: The Lord's Passover

precepts.why:
The lamb had to be “without blemish, a male of the first year”. Peter shows who that lamb is: “the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot: Who verily was foreordained before the foundation of the world, but was manifest in these last times for you”.

The lamb without blemish and without spot points to Christ, who was sinless. He was verily foreordained before the foundation of the world, before ever a lamb was taken in Egypt, but manifest in these last times for the nation of Israel. The Passover lamb, a shadow of things to come, is the shadow of him.

precepts.text: Peter writes to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia: the scattered ones are Israel.
precepts.point: And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men's hands, wood and stone: the wood is the cross of christianity and the stone is the kaaba stone at Mecca. Israel would fall into the heathen religions, christianity and islam, in the lands of the scattering.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia”. The scattered ones are Israel.

Moses prophesied it: “the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen”. Peter writes to those very strangers, scattered among the nations. And it is in the lands of the scattering that Israel would serve gods of wood and stone, the cross of christianity and the kaaba stone at Mecca.

precepts.text: Peter writes to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia.
precepts.point: Israel became strangers in the day they were displaced out of their homeland, as Obadiah says of the day of Jacob's captivity. The peculiar people given the peculiar laws of God is Israel, and that is what is taught to our people today, raising them back up into the understanding of who they are and that we must repent in order to get the kingdom.

note.label: Deuteronomy 14: A Peculiar People and the Clean Foods

precepts.why:
Who is the peculiar people Peter writes to? His letter opens: “Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia”. The chosen generation and peculiar people of his letter are these strangers, scattered through those regions.

Who were those strangers? Acts 2 answers it: Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven, dwelling in the very regions Peter lists, Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia. That is one way to prove who the strangers of the New Testament are.

They are Israel, the peculiar people of Deuteronomy 14:2, become strangers in the day they were displaced out of their homeland.

precepts.text: The spirit that was in the prophets when they were selected to feed the flock of Israel was the spirit of Christ, which testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ.
precepts.point: David was also young when the spirit came on him, and that is nothing new either; the Most High does not choose the ones everybody expects, for the spirit of Christ was in the prophets he selected.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

precepts.why:
“Of which salvation the prophets have enquired and searched diligently, who prophesied of the grace that should come unto you: Searching what, or what manner of time the Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify, when it testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that should follow.”

The spirit that was in the prophets when they were selected to feed the flock of Israel was the spirit of Christ. So when “the Spirit of the Lord came upon David from that day forward”, it was the spirit of Christ in the one the Most High selected.

precepts.text: The prophets have enquired and searched diligently, searching what manner of time the Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify.
precepts.point: The prophets wrote of these things and did not see the time of them.

note.label: Luke 10: The Seventy Sent and the Good Samaritan

precepts.why:
Many prophets and kings desired to see those things which the disciples saw, and did not see them. Peter says the same: “the prophets have enquired and searched diligently, who prophesied of the grace that should come unto you: Searching what, or what manner of time the Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify, when it testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that should follow.”

The prophets wrote of these things and did not see the time of them; they searched what manner of time the Spirit of Christ in them signified. That is why the eyes that saw it are blessed.

precepts.text: Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.
precepts.point: Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. Both are named plainly elsewhere as the word.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
Nicodemus took it literally and asked whether a man can “enter the second time into his mother’s womb, and be born”. Christ answered, “Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.”

Peter tells what that birth is: “Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.” Being born again is by the word of God. Both the water and the Spirit are named plainly elsewhere as the word. It is not a second birth from a mother's womb; it is a birth of incorruptible seed, the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.

precepts.text: Peter writes to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia, elect according to the foreknowledge of the Most High.
precepts.point: People claim Paul wrote to the Romans meaning caucasians, but the scholars say Esau is the forefather of the Roman empire, and the Most High says Jacob have I loved but Esau have I hated. Paul was not writing to the people the Most High hates; he was writing to the Israelites beloved of the Most High who were dispersed and living in Rome as strangers.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Peter writes “to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia, Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father”. The same lands that are on the map in Acts 2, Pontus and Asia among them, and the same word: strangers, people scattered into lands not originally their own.

These strangers are the elect according to the foreknowledge of the Most High, and the elect is Israel. So the strangers of Rome, and the strangers throughout these provinces, are the dispersed Israelites the apostles were sent to.

precepts.text: The Spirit of Christ was always in them, testifying beforehand of his sufferings and the glory to follow.
precepts.point: All who heard were amazed, asking if this is not the same man who destroyed those who called on Christ's name. But Saul increased the more in strength and confounded the Jews at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ. He already knew the scriptures under Gamaliel; when Christ was revealed, everything started to make sense and he took it to another level.

note.label: Acts 9: A Chosen Vessel

precepts.why:
The prophets were “Searching what, or what manner of time the Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify, when it testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that should follow.” The Spirit of Christ was always in them, testifying beforehand of his sufferings and the glory to follow.

That same Spirit was in Saul, separated from his mother's womb, and it is why the scriptures he knew under Gamaliel started to make sense once Christ was revealed. He increased the more in strength, proving from those scriptures that this is very Christ.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why: “Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which according to his abundant mercy hath begotten us again unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,” By the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead: the first begotten of the dead is what gives us that lively hope.

points: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia. So he is not just dealing with Ephesus, Peter is also dealing with other places where the Israelites are scattered.

And Peter's epistles come after his growth, after learning so much and making so many mistakes. When we read Galatians 2, and when we read in John where Christ said Satan desires to have you and sift you as wheat, Peter's epistles are after all that. Satan desires to have you. Brothers, Satan desires to have you. Young men, Satan desires to have you. Sisters, Satan desires to have you. Just like Peter. Peter's epistles come after he finally realised the cock had crowed thrice and Christ looked at him and he wept sore. All of these things are now a part of his understanding, where he can write his epistle with much more clarity than when he was actually walking with Christ.

note.label: Stay in the Spirit

points: Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through sanctification of the Spirit, unto obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: Grace unto you, and peace, be multiplied. Elect. Chosen. Handpicked. According to the foreknowledge of the Father. Before the world was made, that election was already had.

Through sanctification of the Spirit. Definition read in class: in the Bible, sanctification means to be set apart or made holy for God's special use. So how did you go from being in all manner of filth, in all manner of wickedness, to now being here? How did you go from thinking you were going to a tailgate or a football game to actually standing in front of the camp listening for over an hour? Because you were elected, according to God knowing you before that tailgate, before that basketball game, before whatever event you thought you were going to.

note.label: Stay in the Spirit

points: That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire. The whole class we have been talking about gold, and it says your tried faith is valued much more than gold; not just more, much more. People die looking for gold, and what you are going to be is worth more than gold.

Might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ. That is what we are looking for when Christ comes: job well done, my faithful servant; you are worthy of a kingdom. That is what we are all putting this work in for, fighting day and night hoping for a kingdom. I know you are tired; we all get tired, and you are going to push past your limits, but do not give up. Because once you step out, who is to say you can step back in? Once you get off the offramp, who is to say you have enough gas to get back on? Do not play games with God; do not put yourself in a position to lose when you do not have to; do not roll the dice with God.

If you want to hear God laugh, tell him your plan. Your plan is not God's plan. What God has planned for you is keep his commandments and live; that is his only plan for you, and everything else happens because you do what he told you to do. Nothing he puts in your path is there to destroy you; everything adverse that happens to you is because you did it. Your family is out of order because you are out of order; your kids are out of order because you and your wife are out of order; backdoor marriage, you are always going to have a problem, and do not look at leadership about it, because you started out of order.
